children: German defense company Hensoldt still faces a question on the quality of its growth despite delivering good figures on margins and orders in nine-month results, Mwb analyst Jens-Peter Rieck writes in a research note. Growth rests increasingly on its armored vehicles business, which Mwb says is in a temporary cycle of demand that isn't expected to last into the 2030s. Further, the company raised its guidance but without clarifying potential issues at its Zebel logistics center, Rieck says. The company wasn't immediately available for comment. Shares trade 2% lower at 79.80 euros. (sarah.sloat@wsj.com)
